properties.label: Uruk-period southern Mesopotamia
properties.notes: OpenHistoricalMap's 'Uruk culture' relation, which maps only the southern alluvial heartland, not the Uruk expansion into Syria/Iran. Period clipped here to the EBA window; OHM tags the shape -4000..-3100.

properties.label: Early Dynastic Sumer
properties.source: rough outline drawn by an AI agent (not traced from any map), following the extent described in Roaf, Cultural Atlas of Mesopotamia and the Ancient Near East (1990)
properties.notes: The southern alluvium from Sippar/Kish to the head of the Gulf: a mosaic of city-states (Uruk, Ur, Lagash, Umma, Nippur, Kish), not a single polity. The Gulf coast is drawn at its conventional 3rd-millennium position, well north of today's.
properties.reference: Roaf, Cultural Atlas of Mesopotamia and the Ancient Near East (1990)

properties.label: Akkadian Empire
properties.source: rough outline drawn by an AI agent (not traced from any map), following the extent described in Roaf, Cultural Atlas of Mesopotamia and the Ancient Near East (1990)
properties.notes: Sargonic maximum claim, from the Gulf to the upper Euphrates, including Sargonic-governed Susa in Elam. The empire's outer reach is known from royal inscriptions, not from administration; treat the western third as claimed rather than controlled.
properties.reference: Roaf, Cultural Atlas of Mesopotamia and the Ancient Near East (1990)

properties.label: Third Dynasty of Ur
properties.source: rough outline drawn by an AI agent (not traced from any map), following the extent described in Roaf, Cultural Atlas of Mesopotamia and the Ancient Near East (1990)
properties.notes: The bala-taxed core plus the militarised Zagros periphery and Susa, which Shulgi held. The province list is well documented; the drawn outline is a smoothed envelope of it.
properties.reference: Roaf, Cultural Atlas of Mesopotamia and the Ancient Near East (1990)

properties.label: Ebla
properties.source: rough outline drawn by an AI agent (not traced from any map), following the extent described in Bryce, The Routledge Handbook of the Peoples and Places of Ancient Western Asia (2009)
properties.notes: Kingdom of the Ebla palace-G archives. Extent is inferred from the toponyms in the archive and is contested; this is a generous reading covering inland north-west Syria.
properties.reference: Bryce, The Routledge Handbook of the Peoples and Places of Ancient Western Asia (2009)

properties.label: Early Dynastic Egypt
properties.notes: OHM relation; Nile valley and Delta from the Mediterranean to the 1st cataract, no Nubia.

properties.label: Old Kingdom Egypt
properties.notes: OHM relation, same outline as the Early Dynastic one. Old Kingdom activity in Lower Nubia (Buhen) and Sinai is not reflected.

properties.label: Troad (Troy I-III)
properties.source: rough outline drawn by an AI agent (not traced from any map), following the extent described in Bryce, The Routledge Handbook of the Peoples and Places of Ancient Western Asia (2009)
properties.notes: Cultural region around the Troy citadel, not a polity with a border. Drawn as the Biga peninsula plus the Scamander plain.
properties.reference: Bryce, The Routledge Handbook of the Peoples and Places of Ancient Western Asia (2009)

properties.label: Hatti (pre-Hittite central Anatolia)
properties.source: rough outline drawn by an AI agent (not traced from any map), following the extent described in Bryce, The Kingdom of the Hittites, 2nd ed. (2005)
properties.notes: Cultural region of the Hattian-speaking central plateau inside the Halys bend (Alaca Hoyuk, Hattus, Alisar). A convention for 'where the Hittites later were', not an EBA state.
properties.reference: Bryce, The Kingdom of the Hittites, 2nd ed. (2005)

properties.label: Kura-Araxes culture
properties.notes: OHM relation (tagged -3600..-2800 there; period widened here to the conventional span). An archaeological horizon, not a polity; assigned to the Anatolia macro-region although much of it lies in the southern Caucasus.

properties.label: Early Cycladic culture
properties.source: rough outline drawn by an AI agent (not traced from any map), following the extent described in Dickinson, The Aegean Bronze Age (1994)
properties.notes: Island group as a single envelope polygon covering sea as well as land; individual islands are not cut out. Use for grouping, not for point-in-polygon precision.

properties.label: Early Minoan Crete
properties.source: rough outline drawn by an AI agent (not traced from any map), following the extent described in Dickinson, The Aegean Bronze Age (1994)
properties.notes: The island of Crete, coastline simplified to 12 vertices. Prepalatial Crete had no single polity; the polygon stands for the culture area.

properties.label: Yamnaya horizon
properties.notes: OHM relation, simplified from ~89k to ~340 vertices. OHM dates this shape -3300..-3200; the period here is widened to the conventional Yamnaya span (-3300..-2600) so EBA steppe findings match. REVIEWER: confirm you want the wider period.

properties.label: Maykop culture
properties.notes: OHM relation (tagged -3900..-2900 there; narrowed here to the conventional span). North Caucasus piedmont; overlaps Yamnaya both in space and time, which is expected.
